title: Epigastric Pain
correct_orders: Laboratory tests: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Basic Metabolic Panel, Lipase, Amylase
Imaging: Abdominal CT scan with contrast
Order: Order: time-sensitive interventions first; (oxygen, IV access, glucose check)
should_avoid: Order unneccessary invasive procedures without clear indications or prior imaging
Initial orders should not focus on a specific diagnosis as the etiology is unknown

rationale.Laboratory tests: These tests help assess for possible causes of acute abdomen such as infection, pancreatitis, or obstruction
rationale.Abdominal CT scan with contrast: This imaging modality can help identify the source of pain and provide a clearer picture of the abdominal pathology
rationale.Oxygen: The patient is experiencing epigastric pain, which could be a sign of various emergencies such as acute abdomen or cardiac conditions. Oxygen should always be the first intervention to ensure adequate oxygenation.
rationale.Order: Order: time-sensitive interventio: As mentioned in 'How to Use It on Exam Day', immediate action includes ordering oxygen, setting up IV access, and checking glucose levels.

physical_exam: Epigastric Pain — exam tailored to chief complaint on arrival.
Soft, non-distended, no focal peritoneal signs on initial exam.
Alert and oriented unless perfusion or metabolic derangement present.
No acute rash; capillary refill and perfusion assessed.
